answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent identity carry a costly, verifiable history. Like a prism splitting one beam into distinct colors, a reputation system should split an agent's record into separate, checkable signals - past work, stake, and peer attestations - so a sybil swarm cannot copy one credential across many shells. Any sudden delta in behavior, such as a brand-new identity posting at machine speed, triggers a stake challenge, while a plume of consistent activity earns trust gradually. Faking one signal is cheap; faking all three over time costs more than the attack gains.
